key_insight: LLIFT generates semi-synthetic brain MRI with realistic, spatially controlled lesions using only image-level labels, enabling ground-truth datasets for testing XAI methods.
clinical_relevance: This could help researchers benchmark explanation tools on medical images without relying on error-prone pixel-level lesion annotations or unrealistic artificial perturbations.
method: LLIFT learns where to place informative features from binary class labels alone.
LLIFT-GAN uses a custom GAN to transfer pathological features into healthy images.
LLIFT-DM uses diffusion-based inpainting with ControlNet and bounding-box masks.
evidence_signal: On Human Connectome Project brain MRI data, both variants achieved FID scores comparable to the healthy-vs-pathological gap in the dataset, and visual review found the lesions realistic.
watch_item: These are semi-synthetic images for benchmarking, so performance may not fully reflect real-world clinical lesion diversity or downstream XAI behavior.
paper_title: Local Label-Informed Feature Transfer for Generating Ground-Truth Medical Images: A Comparison of GAN- and Diffusion-Based Approaches
